why: An outpost Defend wins the raid the Exchange priced it to win: W8N2's and W7N3's raids near t10000 are each answered by cast bodies, or a free one drafted uncast. Each live row is classed as the engine's, and the run books the energy cast. On 7b15ba9f (before the fix), W7N3's pair (a free body beside a new cast) was walked in 14 ticks apart and lost both; how far apart its bodies reach the raid waits on a Fight event (no fact says it today). Waived by the owner with the centre-first planner, as plan-fragile on main at 53d9148b: with the heap order or the builder scan changed main answered one outpost raid, not two, as this layout does, so one engagement is enough. Evidence (seed 1): an outpost's raid follows the energy dug there; on this layout W8N2 had dug 100,110 by t9800 and its raid landed (Defend opened t9856, drafted t9914, contact t10011, won and closed t10050), while W7N3 had dug 96,288 by t10500 and raised none in the run. No defect: the second raid's tick moves with the dig, not a rule. Seed 2 books no energy cast (liveEnergy 0), as timing: W7N3's dig passes its raid's mark late (100,044 by t10559), its Defend opens t10472, drafts at t10555, and its body fight-10472-1-0 (begun t10524) is still at home when the run ends at t10560
